note: Primitive state forest campground at the north end of Thistledew Lake, with a swimming beach, dock and boat access; one loop under spruce and pine, with sites 1-7 along the shore road. Managed from Scenic State Park. The Thistledew ATV trails are nearby, but ATVs may not be ridden in the campground. --Claude
summary: NOT a horse camp: the DNR names George Washington SF's two horse campgrounds as Togo and Stony Brook; Thistledew is a primitive lake campground (21 drive-in sites, vault toilets, water, swim beach, boat access). Fees $17 tax included, same-day pay, first come. Waterfront lakefront -> lakeview proposed. Manager now Scenic SP (phone added). Note rewritten.
flags: HORSE CAMP CHECK: not a horse camp. DNR forest record: 'This state forest boasts eight camping facilities. Two horse campgrounds, Togo and Stony Brook, have picket lines and pull-through sites. Bear Lake, Button Box, Larson Lake, Lost Lake, Owen Lake, and Thistledew Lake, campgrounds all feature boat launches and fishing opportunities.' Thistledew's own record has no picket lines or horse facilities; the Thistledew Trails are multi-use ATV/horse trails whose parking is on Co. Rd. 542, not at the campground.

OHV (flag only): the facility record names the nearby Thistledew ATV Trail; the map says '**ATV USE IN THE CAMPGROUND IS PROHIBITED** ALL VEHICLES MUST BE TRAILERED IN AND OUT'. A general lake campground with an OHV side (the trail system's parking is elsewhere), so it stays.

WATERFRONT lakefront -> lakeview proposed: the DNR map puts sites 1-7 between the campground road and the Thistledew Lake shore and 15-21 on the lake side of the loop's west bend. On Itasca 2018 leaf-off imagery the spurs of 1-7 (about 47.7992,-93.2368 to 47.7984,-93.2350) sit ~25-35 m back from the water behind unbroken spruce and pine; the west-bend sites are likewise under conifer cover. The one open clearing reaching the water (~47.7993,-93.2394) is at the dock symbol by site 21 and reads as the dock/access opening, not a pad. No site is within ~50 m over open ground.

SITES: count 23 -> 21 (DNR record drive_in_campsites 21; the map numbers 1-21). The old note's 'sites 3-7 best for RVs (one-way loop with a tight spur - no long rigs on the spur)' has no source in the DNR record or map; dropped from the note, no max_rig_ft set.
MANAGER / PHONE: the DNR record now names the manager as Scenic State Park, phone 218-571-2600 (the 2014 map and the old note say McCarthy Beach State Park, 218-254-7979). Phone none -> 218-571-2600.
